menu_options.connection: Set up certificates and local endpoints

connection.title: Local connection settings
connection.description: HA suggests an internal address for its local registration service. Check that the purifier can reach it on the HTTP/HTTPS ports below, and change it if needed. With HA Container, publish those ports and use the host machine's reachable LAN address. Configure HA's MQTT integration separately to use the same broker. Find the MAC and exact model with the setup tool's identify command. Only the 5510 has been hardware verified.

data.server_host: HA registration server LAN hostname or IPv4 address
data.mqtt_host: MQTT broker LAN hostname or IPv4 address

menu_options.generate: Generate a dedicated Winix CA and certificates
menu_options.issuer: Issue certificates with my CA and signing key

generate.title: Generate certificates
generate.description:
HA will create the certificates for your purifier and local servers.

- **Off (default):** Discard the signing key after setup. Replacing certificates later requires a new CA and setting up the purifier again.
- **On:** Save the key in HA so you can issue replacements using the same CA. Renewal is still manual.

Saved keys are unencrypted and may be included in HA backups. Keep those backups private.

data.retain_ca_key: Retain the CA signing key on HA

issuer.title: Use your CA to issue certificates
issuer.description: Paste one PEM CA certificate and its unencrypted RSA signing key. This profile supports one RSA CA directly signing RSA certificates; intermediate chains are not supported. Keys must be at least 2048 bits. A dedicated Winix CA limits the impact of an HA compromise. If retention is off, your imported signing key is not written to disk. Keep your original CA key backup.

data.retain_ca_key: Retain the CA signing key on HA

certificates.title: Import issued certificates
certificates.description: Paste one CA and three certificate/key pairs signed directly by that CA (RSA, at least 2048 bits). The registration and broker certificates need server-auth usage and exact hostname/IP SANs. The device certificate needs client-auth usage and its CN must be the uppercase MAC without separators. CA signing key is optional; provide it only if you want HA to retain it. Private values are not prefilled after errors.

data.retain_ca_key: Retain the supplied CA signing key on HA

confirm.title: Create local installation
confirm.description:
- **Device:** {model} (`{mac}`)
- **MQTT broker:** `{mqtt_host}:{mqtt_port}`
- **Save CA signing key:** {retained}

Select **Submit** to save the installation in HA.

**Next steps**

1. Open **Winix Local → Configure** and download the two setup files.
2. Apply the broker certificate package and topic permissions to your MQTT broker.
3. Follow [Connect the purifier](https://github.com/walero-moon/winix-local#5-connect-the-purifier) on your computer, starting on your usual Wi-Fi.

existing.title: Use an existing installation
existing.description: Enter the MAC for the bundle already installed at /config/winix_local/<MAC>/. Configure HA’s MQTT integration to use the same broker.

error.invalid_settings: Check the exact model, MAC, LAN hosts and distinct registration ports.
error.invalid_certificates: Certificates or keys are invalid, expired, mismatched, or incompatible with the required identity, issuer, hostname or purpose. Re-enter the PEM material; private values were not retained in the form.
error.bundle_exists: An installation already exists for this MAC. Use the existing-bundle path; it will not be replaced.
error.creation_failed: Could not create the private installation. Check directory access and certificate material.

init.title: Download local setup files
init.description:
[Download broker certificate package]({broker}) — contains the broker’s private key. Keep it private. Includes broker-neutral authentication and exact topic-permission requirements; apply these using your broker’s own settings. The CA signing key is never included.

[Download public provisioning configuration]({provision}) — use with `winix-local setup --config provision.json`. It contains no token, private key or Wi-Fi password.

Links expire after five minutes and require your administrator login to remain valid. Reopen this dialog for new links. HA’s MQTT integration must use the same broker. Neither download changes the broker or purifier.

abort.administrator_required: Sign in as a Home Assistant administrator to download setup files.
